1200: They shipped a stack of heavy locked cases under a name that changed every time I asked for it.
1201: They paid extra so I would ask no questions, then acted offended that I had almost asked one.
1202: They handed me cases so heavy I nearly folded, and reminded me they were far too important to carry their own.
1203: They signed the shipping form with a different name than the one on the case, and dared me to notice.
1204: They shipped a dozen locked trunks and asked me to describe them, later, as one very small envelope.
1205: They insisted their bags travel first class while they themselves went somewhere I was paid not to ask about.
1206: They asked me to weigh their cases privately, then tipped me to record a much lighter weight on the form.
1207: They locked each case with three padlocks, then paid me the price of a fourth to forget I had ever seen a key.
1208: They shipped a crate marked fragile that clanked like a treasury, and paid me to write feathers on the label.
1209: They used a false name for the sender, a false name for the receiver, and tipped me to admire both.
1210: They wanted their heavy cases handled with the greatest care and their own presence handled with the greatest secrecy.
1211: They paid for no questions, then answered questions I never asked, all of them wonderfully untrue.
1212: They brought cases too heavy for two clerks and tipped me alone to insist I had barely noticed the weight.
1213: They shipped their locked trunks under a made-up name and demanded a receipt made out to no one at all.
1214: They asked me to stamp the cases urgent, then paid extra to keep the urgent stamp a complete secret.
1215: They handed over case after heavy case and a tip so large I understood I had seen nothing at all.
1216: They wrote a false name on the tag, thought better of it, and wrote a grander false name instead.
1217: They demanded their cases be kept away from all other luggage, as if the other bags were beneath them.
1218: They paid for silence, complete discretion, and no record, then asked me to keep the payment off the record too.
1219: They shipped locked crates that were heavier than they had any right to be, under a name that was lighter than air.
1220: They chartered the fastest boat I own and overpaid me twice, once for the speed and once for my silence.
1221: They asked me to leave their name out of the logbook, then were disappointed the logbook wasn't fancier.
1222: They paid for the swiftest crossing and then complained the sea itself was moving too slowly for them.
1223: They paid me a purse of coins to write nothing in the logbook, then watched the empty page to be sure it stayed empty.
1224: They wanted the whole deck cleared so they could stand alone and be admired by the waves.
1225: They booked my quickest boat, then demanded I repaint the figurehead in their likeness before they would deign to board.
1226: They insisted on the best cabin, the best rope, the best plank, and tipped me not to remember any of it.
1227: They asked me to sail faster than the wind and offered to pay the wind directly if that would help.
1228: They paid a small fortune for the crossing and a larger one to keep it out of every book and every mouth.
1229: They demanded the fastest boat, then more speed, then complained they could still see where they had been.
1230: They overpaid for my quickest craft and asked me to throw the logbook overboard once we were done.
1231: They wanted no entry, no witnesses, no memory, and then bragged about how discreet they were being.
1232: They pressed extra coins into my hand to sail faster and extra coins to say the boat had never left the dock.
1233: They chartered the boat, tipped the crew, and asked that the sea keep no record of their passing either.
1234: They insisted their name never touch the logbook, then signed it grandly on my sleeve out of habit.
1235: They demanded a faster boat, and when I explained I only owned the one, asked to speak to whoever owned a faster one.
1236: They overpaid for speed and secrecy, then wanted a receipt proving how much secrecy they had bought.
1237: They asked to leave no trace in the logbook and tipped so heavily that the tip left a trace instead.
1238: They asked me to forget the whole voyage, then filled it with stories I was plainly meant to remember forever.
1239: They chartered my quickest boat, overpaid the fare, and seemed insulted a vessel this fine still had to touch water.
